title: SourceArtifactV5
description: A supplied source as a durable identity across every byte state it ever has. This node exists so the question 'is this the same document?' can be answered separately from 'is this the same bytes?' — only the second is hashable, and conflating them is how a proof silently carries forward onto a source that was replaced. Emitted as a `source.artifact` node by `register_sources()` in `scripts/wi.py` during `wi ingest`; consumed by `wi anchor`, `wi impact`, `wi graph` and the `sources/sources.lock` member of a `.wiab` bundle. The v5.0 core populates `logical_id`, `path`, `title` and `media_type` only; `confidentiality`, `rights` and `identity` are specified in references/v5/WORKSPACE.md and references/v5/RIGHTS_AND_CONSENT.md and are declared by a human, never inferred.

logical_id.description: Derived by `logical_id("source", <file name>)`. Note that it keys on the file name, not the full path or the bytes: two versions of the same file share this id, which is exactly what makes supersession expressible.

path.description: POSIX-normalized path the source was ingested from, relative to the workspace root where possible. Provenance and human navigation; the anchor system addresses bytes, not paths.

title.description: Display name for the source, defaulting to the file name. What appears in a proof line a reader will actually read.

media_type.description: IANA media type of the source as ingested. `wi ingest` records `text/plain` for every source it can read as text in v5.0; binary adapters are specified and report `WI_SOURCE_UNSUPPORTED` rather than guessing.

confidentiality.description: Disclosure classification that rides with this source through every derived object. It governs what a bundle profile may include: a `restricted` source's bytes must never appear in a `full` bundle. Specified in references/v5/WORKSPACE.md; not populated by the v5.0 ingest path.

rights.description: On what footing this source is held and what that footing permits. Present so that 'may we redistribute this?' is a recorded answer rather than an assumption made at bundle time.

identity.description: Whether an identifiable person appears in this source and on what basis they appear. Kept separate from `rights` because permission to use a document and consent from a person depicted in it are different permissions from different parties.

logical_id.description: A UUID-shaped, content-derived logical identity produced by `logical_id()`.

timestamp.description: ISO-8601 instant with an explicit UTC offset.

confidentiality.description: `public` may appear anywhere; `internal` may not leave the organization; `confidential` may not leave the workspace in a bundle profile that carries bytes; `restricted` may not have its bytes carried by any profile, and only hash-only or approved redacted excerpts may reference it.

rights.description: The rights block. `unknown` is a legitimate value and must never be silently upgraded: no inference path exists from `unknown` to any other value, and a basis changes only by a recorded human declaration.

basis.description: On what footing the source is held. `unknown` records the true state — that nobody has established the footing — and is a value a gate can act on, unlike a guess.

scope.description: What the basis actually permits. Free text plus structured facets, because a gate can evaluate the facets and a human needs the sentence.

text.description: The permission in the operator's own words, as declared.

publication.description: Whether the basis permits publishing content derived from this source.

redistribution.description: Whether the basis permits shipping the source bytes themselves. A `full` bundle requires this to be true for every source it carries.

derivative_works.description: Whether the basis permits derivative works.

territory.description: Territorial limit of the basis, or `unrestricted`.

expires_at.description: When the basis stops being true, or null when it does not expire. A date in the past is a gate condition, not a footnote.

declared_by.description: Actor id of the person who declared this basis. A rights basis is only ever produced by a person.

identity.description: Whether a person is recognizable in the source, and on what footing they appear.

contains_identifiable_person.description: Recorded as a three-valued string rather than a boolean precisely so that `unknown` is expressible. A boolean would force a guess at ingestion, which is the moment the person entering it knows least.

consent_basis.description: On what footing the identifiable person appears. `self` is the author appearing in their own material; `public_figure_context` is the narrowest of the non-consent bases and does not extend past the context recorded here.

subject_label.description: A pseudonymous handle for the person, used in reports so a proof line never has to print a real name.

consent_record.description: Object reference (`obj:sha256:...`) to the stored consent artifact, so the basis points at a document rather than at a memory.
